AffixDoc.description:
A prefix or suffix: one string, or an ordered list of conditional parts.

The list form is the concatenation rule. Every entry whose condition holds contributes its text, in the order the author wrote them, so independent conditions each add their own piece: a whole marking takes a separator when one category is present and a leading word when another category holds a particular concept, and both when both hold. Nesting can only express the all-or-nothing case, and enumerating the combinations as alternatives costs one option per subset.

A part whose condition is false contributes nothing, and an affix whose parts all contribute nothing is an absent affix: it does not frame an otherwise empty result.

AffixPartDoc.description:
One piece of a conditional affix: text, and when it is written.

An entry with no `when` is unconditional and always contributes.

when.description: When this part is written. Absent means always.

AlternativesFieldDoc.description:
One semantic field with several possible representations.

Not first-match-wins: exactly one binding is active for any given state, and two active at render is a representation conflict, never a silent pick. Inside this field a descendant may stand for an already-implied, value-free ancestor, following the full parent graph; it never hides an explicit, distinct, or contradictory instruction.

alternatives.description: The possible representations of this one field.

attribute.description: `xml-attributes` syntax only: the attribute's local name.

name.description: Human label for the field. Required on groups and alternatives, because a `joins` entry and a diagnostic both have to be able to name them.

prefix.description: Written once before the field's nonempty result.

prefix_aliases.description:
Spellings of this field's prefix that are read and never written.

A format writes one spelling of a line and documents in the wild carry more than one. A block whose classifier line opens `Classified By: ` also arrives spelled out for a derivative classifier, and a reader that accounts for every character refuses that spelling unless the format names it. Two `alternatives` that can both write one state are a conflict by design and never a winner by order, and a `Recognizer` describes a whole region rather than one line inside a block.

This is the tolerant half of the tree, written down. The canonical pass reads `prefix` and nothing else; a spelling named here is admitted only by the tolerant pass, beside the case difference, the declared alias, a concept's spelling in another of its views and the separator substitution it already admits, and every use is reported as an `alias` correction against the characters it read. The render side never reads this, which is what "never written" means. A format that declares none reads only `prefix`.

Only meaningful beside `prefix`, and no two fields of one format may claim one spelling, as a prefix or as an alias of one. A line that opens two fields is not a reading a format can settle, and nothing here is settled by declaration order.

required.description:
Whether the field standing empty is a state of this group at all.

Every field is optional by default, and on the read side that default is load-bearing in a way it is easy to miss: a group all of whose fields may stand empty reads any one of them on its own. A format that binds two categories beside a level therefore also reads a bare level, and becomes a rival account of text another format already reads whole. The alternative is not a tie-break, because nothing here is settled by declaration order, position or count. It is saying the thing the document could not say: a reading in which this field matched nothing is not a reading of this group.

Symmetric, because a representation that cannot be read is not one. Set here, the field is bound in every reading of the group that encloses it, and a state holding nothing for it is a state the group does not write: the group comes out empty, the facts its other fields would have carried are reported omitted, and another field or another format writes them. An omission, not a conflict: the group declined, and declining is what a format that does not represent a state is supposed to do.

The same word at a format's top level says it of the whole format, whose fields are one sequence. Inside `alternatives` it belongs to the option it is written in and says nothing about the others, because each option is a whole representation of the field and they do not share a reading.

It is a statement about this group's shape, never about the concept the field binds and never about whether a marking is well formed: a category that must be filled for a marking to make sense is `required` on the category, which is a different question with a different answer.

separator.description: What this field joins: its own values on a category field, its nonempty children on a group.

separator_aliases.description:
Spellings of this field's separator that are read and never written.

The sibling of `prefix_aliases`, one level down: a prefix says where a field opens and a separator says where one of its values ends, and a document in the wild spells the second as freely as the first. A list a format writes with `, ` arrives joined by `; ` or by a bare space, and a reader that accounts for every character reads the whole run as one value rather than quietly guessing a boundary.

Not the same as the substitutions the tolerant pass already makes. Those are spacing and de-doubling variants of the declared separator, and they deliberately invent no boundary the declared separator does not already put in the same place. This is the author saying that these other characters are that boundary, in this field, which is a statement only the document can make.

Tolerant pass only, never written, and every use is reported as a `separator` correction naming the characters read and the separator the format writes instead: the same correction a spacing substitution carries, because it is the same claim about the same boundary. The render side never reads this.

Only meaningful beside `separator`. A spelling named here may not be another field's declared separator or another field's prefix in the same format: a boundary that is also a field's own syntax is not a reading the format can settle, and nothing here is settled by declaration order.

suffix.description: Written once after the field's nonempty result.

view.description: Concept view for this field, overriding the enclosing view.

when.description: When this field applies. One predicate, read by both sides: the field is written only when it holds, and a reading of the input that would make it false is not a reading of this field.

AttributionDoc.description: Provenance attached to every external source. Mirrors the runtime `Attribution` declared in `./source.ts`; redeclared here so the YAML schema can validate it without depending on the runtime source contract.

license.description: SPDX identifier or short license token, such as `CC-BY-4.0`.

licenseUrl.description: Canonical URL where the license terms can be inspected.

name.description: Display name of the upstream source.

CategoryDoc.description: A category: a dimension of a marking that groups related concepts.

allowed_concepts.description: If set, only these concept IDs are valid (overrides categories[] membership).

citation.description:
Where in the governing document this category was read from. Free text, e.g. `2016 IC Markings Register, Table 3 row 24`.

Provenance only: nothing parses it, matches on it, or renders it.

collapse_groups.description: When true, a group concept present together with every one of its members is rendered alone, with the members folded into it. A member named by `group_exclude` does not count toward that check. A group missing any member is rendered as stated, beside whichever members are present.

default_concept.description: Default concept when this category is empty; a string is unconditional.

format_hint.description: Advisory shape of this category's free-text values, for a host that wants to hint at the expected form in an input box. Provenance and UI only: nothing parses it, matches on it, or validates against it. A value's real shape is its concept's `text_input.encoding`.

group_exclude.description: Concept ID excluded from the "all members present" check for collapse.

hierarchy_root.description: When true, the category grades its concepts by severity `rank`: every concept it grades must declare one or the scheme fails to load, and a coverage comparison counts a whole-marking concept here as covering a part's concept of equal or lower rank. It does not change rendering.

position.description:
Position of the category within the rendered output (lower = earlier).

Any number, not only a whole one: a fraction is how a category is slotted between two others without renumbering the rest.

position_overrides.description: Numeric positions keyed by concept ID, used by this category's `position` sort instead of the concept's resolved position. Other concepts retain their own positions. Equal positions use the next sort key, then declared concept order. These values affect only this category and never severity.

required.description: Whether at least one concept must be present for a valid marking.

rollup.description:
Rollup operator used when aggregating multiple markings.

`pipeline` means the category is resolved by an entry in `scheme.rollup_pipelines[]`.

scopes.description: Scope IDs this category is visible in.

single.description: When true, only one concept can be selected.

sort.description: Sort order for concepts within this category during rendering.

suppress_if_subset_of.description: Suppress this category if its concept set is a subset of another category's set.

views.description: Additional display views keyed by view name.

attribute.description: `xml-attributes` syntax only: the attribute's local name.

concept.description: Narrow the binding to one concept: a fixed slot such as a header.

each.description: Affix written around each value, as opposed to once around all of them.

exclude_concepts.description: Concepts bound by another field of this format, excluded here so the two bindings are disjoint. Selection metadata, not parser precedence.

name.description: Human label for the field. Required on groups and alternatives, because a `joins` entry and a diagnostic both have to be able to name them.

tiers.description: How a tiered concept composes inside this field.

unspelled.description:
Concepts of this field's category its view deliberately does not spell.

A `view_only` field leaves out a concept its view has no spelling for, and a scheme check warns about each one, because most often the author meant the field to carry it and forgot the spelling. view.description: Concept view for this field, overriding the enclosing view.

view_only.description:
Whether this field writes only what its own view spells.

A concept's spelling in a view falls back to `default`, which is what lets a scheme name a view on the concepts that differ in it and leave the rest alone. A field standing for a closed set cannot take that fallback: an attribute whose published vocabulary enumerates exactly what it accepts has no spelling for anything else, and writing the `default` one puts a token in it that nothing reads back.

Set here, a concept with no spelling in this field's view is left out of this field and reported as omitted; every other field still writes it, and the render stands, because an omission is the answer a closed set gives rather than a fact the output lost. Recognition is unchanged: this engine reads more tolerantly than it writes everywhere, and a field told what it may write has not been told to stop understanding things.

It is a statement about the field's vocabulary, never about the concept, and never about which of two readings is right.

CategoryFieldDoc.description:
A field bound to a category, optionally narrowed to particular concepts.

Written one of two ways, and a field that does neither has no binding at all: it names the category, or it names a concept that determines one. Naming a concept that belongs to exactly one category makes `category` redundant, and writing it out anyway puts two facts in the document where one decides the other. A concept in several categories is a real choice and the field has to make it, which is why the second form still accepts `category`.

default.description: The label used when no other view is asked for.

CategoryLabelDoc.description:
Category label: either a plain string or a view-keyed map.

The map form lets a category carry alternate labels per render format (e.g. `{ default: 'Access Tier', abbr: 'tier' }`).

ChildrenOfSelectorDoc.description:
Every concept whose `parents` list names a concept.

`{ children_of: PROGRAM }` stands for every concept whose `parents` list names `PROGRAM`. Only direct children count: a concept whose parent is itself a child of `PROGRAM` is not one. The set is read from the scheme as composed, after every layer has added and removed its concepts, so a layer that adds a child needs no rule of its own, and a scheme with no children of `PROGRAM` has an empty set. The children are the concepts the scheme declares, inline or from a source it holds in full; a scheme whose concepts are only looked up one at a time cannot list them, and refuses a selector at load.

Where a rule needs one of its targets (`require_any`), an empty set fails every marking the rule fires on: a concept that requires one of its children is refused while it has none.

children_of.description: The concept whose direct children are the targets.

CompositeFieldDoc.description:
One component of a `composite` encoding.

A `concept` component names words inside the value. It identifies them; it does not assert them as top-level facts of the marking.

concepts.description: `type: concept`: the concept ids this component may name.

required.description: Whether the component must be present. Default true.

type.description: Whether the component is free text or a reference to known concepts.

view.description: `type: concept`: the view the component is written in.

ConceptApplicabilityDoc.description: Applicability metadata: which organizations use this concept.

organizations.description: Identifiers of the organizations that use this concept.

ConceptCategoryMappingDoc.description:
One category membership in a concept mapping, applied only to the records that satisfy its condition.

A bare string entry in `categories` gives every record the same membership. That is right for a category every record belongs to and wrong for one that holds for most of them, which is why this form exists: the membership is still declared once, and the condition says which records it reaches.

`when` and `unless` are conditions over the record. A bare field holds when it is present and not empty; `field == 'X'`, `field != 'X'` and `field in ['X', 'Y']` compare projected values as strings. Declare one or the other, whichever reads as the plainer sentence.

id.description: Expression for the category id, or ids, this entry contributes.

unless.description: Apply the membership to every record except those this condition holds for.

when.description: Apply the membership only to records this condition holds for.

ConceptColor.description:
Portable scheme-default display colors, carried as a text/background pair so contrast is authored together. In category mode they are declared only on concepts in the category named by `render.color_from`; consuming hosts may override them.

Both values are CSS hex (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`). The pair travels together so a host never composes one authored color against an unknown surface (the white-on-white failure mode).

background.description: Background color as a CSS hex string.

text.description: Text/foreground color as a CSS hex string.

ConceptDoc.description: A concept: the core unit of a scheme.

aliases.description: Alternative strings that parse to this concept (case-insensitive).

categories.description: Category IDs this concept belongs to.

citation.description:
Where in the governing document this concept was read from. Free text, e.g. `NARA CUI Registry, General Privacy, retrieved 2026-07-25` or `32 CFR 2002.20(b)(1)`.

Provenance only: nothing parses it, matches on it, or renders it. Distinct from `definition` (what the concept means) and `guidance` (what the controlling authority says about handling it).

color.description: Portable scheme-default display color pair (`{ background, text }`, both CSS hex). In category mode it is allowed only on concepts in the category named by `render.color_from`. Hosts may override it.

definition.description: Human-readable definition of this concept from its governing authority.

deprecated_replacement.description: Concept ID that should be used instead of this deprecated concept.

guidance.description: Usage guidance for when and how to apply this concept.

id.description: Unique concept identifier within the scheme.

input_aliases.description: Aliases that mean this concept only in a stated position.

members.description: For group concepts: the member concept IDs.

metadata.description: Opaque host metadata carried with the concept. The engine neither reads nor interprets it; it travels so a host can hang its own record on a concept without a second file keyed by id.

notices.description: Regulatory or handling notices attached to this concept.

parents.description: Broader concept IDs forming a hierarchy chain.

position.description: Position spec: relative ordering within a category.

rank.description: Rank spec: severity ordering for max/min rollup.

scopes.description: Scope IDs this concept is visible in.

stands_for_whole.description:
A category whose values this concept stands for: the values the whole holds in it.

Some schemes let a part leave out a list because it is the same as its whole's, and write a word in its place. The concept is that word. When a part holding it is read against a whole, the part takes the whole's values in the named category, so its rules judge the list the word stands for. The concept stays in the part, and a format that sets `omit_whole_values` writes the part back the way it was read. A part read without a whole, or one that writes values of its own in the category, takes nothing; whether a word with nothing behind it is an error is the scheme's call, made in its own rules. In a rollup the word goes through its own category's rollup like any other concept.

Names a category declared in the same scheme.

supersedes.description: Concept IDs that this concept supersedes.

synonyms.description: Locale-specific display labels: locale code → display string.

tier.description: Tier label. Marks this concept as a partial marking that must attach to a parent.

default.description: The representation used when no other view is asked for.

views.description:
Display representations keyed by view name; must include 'default'. A plain string expands to all view keys.

A view value may carry one placeholder, `{value}`, which the renderer fills with the assertion's free-text value. Any other placeholder is invalid and causes a compile error. Alternate representations live in typed text-input encodings, which define parsing and rendering per declared view.

A value that has to print in more than one shape per view says so in its own `text_input.encoding`, which states both directions. A `calendar-date` stores one canonical spelling and names a per-view spelling; a `composite` names its components.

ConceptGroupDoc.description: A named collection of concepts. It groups concepts for people reading or browsing the scheme; it has no effect on parsing, rules or rendering.

concept_ids.description: The concepts in the group, by id.

id.description: Unique group id within the scheme.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to the id.

ConceptMappingDoc.description: Mapping spec for an external concept source: declarative projection of upstream records into canonical Concept fields. Expression strings use a small JMESPath subset: field paths, literal and wildcard indexes, quoted literals, `@`, `+` concatenation, and `??` for the first present operand.

concept.description: How each record's fields project onto a concept.

aliases.description: Expressions for the concept's aliases, one per entry.

categories.description: The categories each record's concept belongs to: an expression or list of expressions for category ids, or conditional memberships.

citation.description: Expression for the provenance citation (concept.citation on the output). A record that carries its own citation keeps it; a source whose citation is the same for every record can supply a literal.

definition.description: Expression for a human-readable definition (concept.definition on the output).

deprecated.description: Expression that marks the concept deprecated when it yields a truthy value.

guidance.description: Expression for usage guidance text (concept.guidance on the output).

id.description: Expression for the concept id. A record that yields none is refused.

name.description: Expression for the display name. Falls back to the id.

parents.description: Expression for the concept's parent concept ids: one id or a list of them.

position.description: Expression for the concept's numeric render position. A value that does not convert to a number gives position 0.

rank.description: Expression for the concept's numeric rank. A value that does not convert to a number leaves the concept unranked.

search.description: Declares that the upstream supports a search call and names the query parameter that carries the search term. Presence infers `capabilities.search` and `capabilities.prefixMatch`, and supplies the transport's default search parameter name unless `queryParams.search` overrides it.

queryParam.description: Name of the query parameter that carries the search term.

views.description: Expressions for the concept's display representations, keyed by view name. The `default` view falls back to the name.

omit.description:
Condition, in the same expression subset as `record`, evaluated against each upstream record. A record it holds for is dropped before any concept is projected, so the omitted records are absent from enumerate, count, search and resolve alike.

Use it when the upstream snapshot is the right source of truth and a few of its records have no representation in the scheme being built. Every field the condition names must exist on the records, or the source fails to load.

record.description: Selector for the array of records on a transport response.

ConceptNoticeDoc.description: A regulatory or handling notice attached to a concept: the text the marking requires, plus how it is categorized, whether it is mandatory, and an optional condition. Where the text is placed in a document is the host's convention, not part of the scheme.

condition.description: Concept ID: only show this notice when this concept is also present.

required.description: Whether this notice MUST be displayed (regulatory requirement).

views.description:
The value this notice is registered under in a view's own notice vocabulary, keyed by view name, e.g. `{ ism: 'RD' }`.

Only for a view that has such a vocabulary. A view with no entry here carries the notice unregistered, which is what a view says when its vocabulary does not enumerate this notice. The registration sits on the notice rather than on a format because it is a property of the notice: a concept carrying two notices registers each one separately, and a format that writes the notice is not the thing that names it.

ConditionDoc.description:
A single condition in a rule's `when:` block.

Rule conditions name their category via `category`; structured `when:` blocks elsewhere (categories, render formats, rollup pipelines, filters) use `category_id`. The shorthand `is:` packs an operator+value into one string (e.g. `'has_content'`, `'count_eq 1'`). `has:` is shorthand for `operator: has_concept, value: <id>`.

category.description: Category ID to evaluate against (rule conditions).

category_id.description: Category ID to evaluate against (structured `when:` blocks).

operator.description: Explicit operator (used when `is`/`has` is not a fit).

target.description: Which assertion set to evaluate: 'self' (default), 'context' (whole marking), or 'contributors' (every set that fed an aggregate; the condition holds only when all of them satisfy it).

value.description: Operand for the operator: a concept id for the concept tests, a category id for `subset_of` and `shares_concept_with`, and a number for the `count_*`, `min_order` and `min_rank` tests.

ConditionOperator.description: Comparison operator for a structured `when:` condition.

ConditionalDefaultConceptDoc.description: A category default applied only when its condition holds.

concept.description: Concept ID to assert when the category is empty.

when.description: Evaluated against assertions after inference and before any category defaults are added, independently of category declaration order. An unresolved condition does not fill the default.

DefaultViewByRoleDoc.description:
A surface's default view for each role, where the right default depends on whether the marking is a whole or a part.

`{ whole: full, part: short }` writes a whole marking in `full` and a part in `short`. `whole` is required and `part` falls back to it, so `{ whole: block }` and `{ whole: block, part: block }` mean what the view id `block` means. A marking with no role is written as a whole, the same way the engine reads a call that names no role as a call about the whole marking. Each value is one of the surface's own views, and no other key is allowed.

Where `part` names a view of its own, that view is a view of part markings and the `whole` view is not, so a marking written in either is read back as that view and written in it again: a part, as a part, and a whole, as a whole or as a marking with no role. The exception is text that a form of a view of another role writes the same way: it reads back with no role, as `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` decides, and a request that names neither an output nor a role writes it as a whole.

part.description: The view a part marking is written in. Where the surface has views of part markings, one of them, and a view of part markings whenever it is not the `whole` view. Absent, the `whole` view.

whole.description: The view a whole marking, or a marking with no role, is written in. Where the surface has views of whole markings, one of them.

EachAffixDoc.description: Affix written around every value of a field, as opposed to once around all of them.

EmbeddedMarkingStyleDoc.description: Embedded-marking style: pattern wrapping an inner marking in free text.

auto_insert.description: When the host UI should auto-prompt for a marking.

pattern.description: Regex with one capture group around the inner marking text.

template.description: Output template when re-emitting the wrapper. `{marking}` is replaced. Required: an insertion has to round-trip through this scheme's own `pattern`, so the engine cannot supply a wrapper syntax of its own.

ExternalSourceAuth.description:
Request-level authentication on an external source. `flow` selects the registered handler (Basic, Bearer, a named header, AWS-SigV4, OAuth2 client credentials) that decorates each request; the credential refs are provider-specific opaque ids that are resolved server-side.

Certificates are not request-level. A client certificate for mutual TLS, and a CA bundle for a private upstream, belong to the connection and are declared in the source's `tls` block.

accessKeyRef.description: AWS access key ref, used by `aws-sigv4`.

params.description: Optional scopes / region / token endpoint params, provider-specific.

secretKeyRef.description: AWS secret access key ref, used by `aws-sigv4`.

ExternalSourceCapabilities.description: Capability hints declared on an external source. The compiler infers defaults from the mapping shape; an explicit block overrides inference.

ancestorsOf.description: Whether the upstream can list a concept's ancestors.

childrenOf.description: Whether the upstream can list a concept's children.

count.description: Whether the upstream reports how many records it holds. Used by authoring tools.

enumerate.description: Whether the upstream can be browsed page by page. Used by authoring tools, not by the runtime.

prefixMatch.description: Whether the upstream answers a prefix lookup.

resolveAliases.description: How the upstream resolves an alias to a concept: `exact` for literal matches, `fuzzy` for tolerant ones, or `none` when it cannot.

search.description: Whether the upstream answers a free-text search.

style.description: The upstream answers in a single response.

pageParam.description: Name of the query parameter that carries the page number.

start.description: The number of the first page, usually `0` or `1`.

style.description: The upstream pages by page number: `start` first, then one more per page, until a page comes back empty.

offsetParam.description: Name of the query parameter that carries the record offset.

style.description: The upstream pages by record offset: `0` first, then the previous offset plus the records that page returned, until a page comes back empty.

cursorParam.description: Name of the query parameter that carries the cursor.

nextField.description: Dot-path in the response body to the next page's cursor.

style.description: The upstream pages by an opaque cursor it returns. The read ends at the first page whose response names no next cursor.
The upstream links the next page in its `Link` response header. The read ends at the first page whose response links no next page.

ExternalSourcePagination.description:
Pagination shape declared on an HTTP transport.

A read follows the declared style until the style's last page, and fails rather than return a partial set when it cannot get there: a failed page, a repeated continuation or page, or a read past the host's page, record or time limit. The page size, for every style, is the `queryParams.pageSize` parameter.

The `page` and `offset` styles compute the next request themselves, so an empty page is the only page that ends the read; a short page does not, because the upstream's page size is not something the read trusts. The `cursor` and `link-header` styles follow the continuation the upstream returns, and the read ends at the first page that names none.

ExternalSourceQueryParams.description: Upstream-specific query-parameter names for an HTTP external source. Each field overrides the transport's built-in default name (`search` → `q`, `prefix` → `prefix`, `scope` → `scope`, `pageSize` → `pageSize`) so a customer mapping an upstream that searches via `?query=` or `?filter=` isn't stuck with the transport's own convention. Page continuation parameters belong to the `pagination` block.

pageSize.description: Name of the query parameter that carries the page size, for every pagination style. Default `pageSize`.

prefix.description: Name of the query parameter that carries a prefix to match. Default `prefix`.

scope.description: Name of the query parameter that carries a scope. Default `scope`.

search.description: Name of the query parameter that carries a search term. Default `q`.

ExternalSourceSpec<ConceptMappingDoc>.description: The body of an `external:` block on a concept / guide-rule / access source. The mapping field is one of `ConceptMappingDoc`, `RuleMappingDoc`, or `AccessMappingDoc` depending on which artifact this block belongs to.

auth.description: Request-level authentication, applied to each request.

capabilities.description: Capability overrides. When omitted, inferred from `mapping`.

grantId.description: The publisher's opaque reference (`grantId:<uuid>`) to the sharing grant under which it read the source `srcref` names. Provenance only; the engine accepts it and does not act on it.

id.description: Stable identifier for this source within the containing artifact. Required when multiple external sources appear on the same scheme; the loader synthesizes `external-${i}` when the field is absent.

liveFetch.description: How the publisher obtained the records it published for this source: `true` when it read the upstream as it composed the artifact, `false` (the default) when it used a stored snapshot, named by `snapshotRef`. Provenance only; the engine accepts it and does not act on it.

mapping.description: Declarative projection from foreign records into canonical shape.

mappingHash.description: The publisher's anchor over this spec block: SHA-256 hex of its canonical sorted-key JSON serialization, excluding this field. Whoever publishes the artifact writes it. The engine recomputes it when it loads the Context and refuses to load on a mismatch, so a block edited after publication is caught. Absent means the block carries no anchor and nothing is checked.

pagination.description: HTTP-only knobs. Ignored for non-http transports.

queryParams.description: HTTP-only: override the transport's default query-parameter names.

burst.description: Most requests allowed in one window.

windowMs.description: Length of the window, in milliseconds.

recordsPath.description: Dot-path into the JSON response body that locates the records array (HTTP only). Omit when the response body is itself the array. Use this for upstreams that wrap their payload, e.g. GeoJSON `FeatureCollection.features`, ArcGIS REST `features`, Elasticsearch `hits.hits`.

snapshotId.description:
Optional pin on the records this source serves: the sha256 records digest the source reports for them, written `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits (the pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`). When it is set, the engine loads the artifact only if the source reports the same digest, so an artifact version is immutable around it. To absorb new data from upstream, mint a new artifact version with the new digest.

A label such as a release name never matches and is refused; it belongs in `attribution.citation`. Omit the pin for a best-effort live source that cannot report a stable digest.

snapshotRef.description: The publisher's content-addressed reference to the stored snapshot the records came from, when `liveFetch` is `false`. Provenance only; the engine accepts it and does not act on it.

source.description: URI for the upstream: http(s), file://, or inline:// (rare).

srcref.description: The publisher's opaque reference (`srcref:<uuid>`) to a source another organization shared with it, when the records came through such a share. Provenance only; the engine accepts it and does not act on it.

tls.description: HTTP only: the connection's TLS settings (a private CA, a client certificate for mutual TLS). Independent of `auth`, so a source can present a client certificate and a bearer token together. A source whose only credential is its client certificate has `tls` and no `auth`.

ExternalSourceTls.description:
TLS settings for an HTTP external source's connections. They apply to requests to `source` and to same-origin redirects. Any `tls` setting pins the source to its origin, so a cross-origin redirect is refused. Server verification is always on and cannot be turned off here.

Declare at least one field, and give `keyPassphraseRef` only together with `clientCertAndKeyRef`. The block is valid only on an `http` transport whose `source` is an `https:` URL; the runtime refuses it anywhere else when it builds the source.

caBundleRef.description: PEM CA bundle that verifies the upstream server certificate. Resolves to a string-secret. When set, it replaces the platform's default roots for this source. The material is public, but it is referenced rather than inlined so the deployment can rotate it without a new artifact version.

clientCertAndKeyRef.description: Client certificate and private key presented in the handshake (mutual TLS). Resolves to a cert-and-key-pair.

keyPassphraseRef.description: Passphrase for an encrypted private key in `clientCertAndKeyRef`. Resolves to a string-secret. Requires `clientCertAndKeyRef`. Leave it unset when the pair already carries its passphrase; supplying both is refused.

ExternalSourceTransport.description: Discriminated transport union for an external source. `transport` is inferred from the URI scheme when omitted (`https://` → `http`, `file://` → `file`, no scheme → `inline-data`); explicit values win.

FieldDoc.description: One field of a format. Exactly one binding shape per field.

FilterDoc.description: A view filter: view-time concept filter consulted by render and suggest.

formats.description:
Render formats the filter applies in, by format ID. Absent or empty means every format, the same convention as `in`. Use it when a concept is legitimate in the marking but has no encoding in one output format.

Only render consults this; `suggest()` is never format-scoped.

keep.description: Concept or category IDs to keep (whitelist) when the filter fires.

remove.description: Concept or category IDs to remove when the filter fires.

FixedAttributeFieldDoc.description:
An attribute whose value the format fixes, written when a predicate holds.

Every other field carries a fact out of the state and writes it. This one writes the literal the document names, and it is read back as a check that the same predicate holds: finding the attribute says the state satisfies `when`, and an input that carries it while the predicate fails is not a reading of this format. It binds no concept, and that is the point. A structured representation can require a flag attribute that says something about the representation rather than about the marking, and binding a concept to it would make one way of writing a state hold a fact another way of writing the same state does not.

`when` is required. A fixed attribute written for every state says nothing about any of them and the read side learns nothing from finding it, which makes it a constant belonging to the format's syntax rather than a field.

`xml-attributes` syntax only.

name.description: Human label for the field, for `joins` entries and diagnostics.

output_surfaces.description: The surfaces whose output this attribute belongs to, each named once. Required in a format that writes more than one surface, because the attribute binds no category to say. Omitted in a format that writes one surface, it is that surface. It decides only which output writes the attribute: reading it, and what its `when` can see, are unchanged.

value.description: The literal written as the attribute's value.

when.description: When the attribute is written, and what finding it asserts on the way back in.

fields.description: The fields, in the order they are written.

id.description: Format identifier. `render.default` and the views of `render.surfaces` refer to it, and callers name it as an input format. In a scheme without `render.surfaces` it is also an output format. In a scheme with them it is a form of one view on each surface it serves, and it names an output only when exactly one view names it; see `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces`.

joins.description: Separators for particular boundaries between adjacent top-level fields.

mode.description: Layout: `inline` runs the fields together, `block` puts each on its own line.

omit_defaults.description: Leave assertions with `source: 'default'` out of the printed output. A print filter only: every condition in this format still sees the real, unfiltered state.

omit_empty.description: Skip empty fields. Defaults to true for `block`, false for `inline`.

omit_whole_values.description:
Write a part's stand-in in place of the values it took from its whole.

A part that holds a stand-in (a concept that declares `stands_for_whole`) and was read against a whole holds the whole's values in the category the stand-in names. This format leaves those values out, so the part is written back with the word it was read with. It applies only to a part read on its own: a rollup is a whole, and is always written with its values. A print filter only, like `omit_defaults`: every condition in this format still sees the values.

prefix.description: Written once before the nonempty whole.

separator.description: Joins the nonempty top-level fields. Required once there is more than one field and no `joins` entry covers the boundary.

separator_aliases.description:
Spellings of this format's own separator that are read and never written.

The same word as on a field, said of the boundary between the format's top-level fields. See `FieldCommonDoc.separator_aliases`: tolerant pass only, never written, every use a `separator` correction, and no spelling here may be another field's separator or another field's prefix.

suffix.description: Written once after the nonempty whole.

surface.description: The semantic part of a marking this format writes: a scheme scope id. `surfaces` is absent.

view.description: Default concept view for fields that do not name one.

fields.description: The fields, in the order they are written.

id.description: Format identifier. `render.default` and the views of `render.surfaces` refer to it, and callers name it as an input format. In a scheme without `render.surfaces` it is also an output format. In a scheme with them it is a form of one view on each surface it serves, and it names an output only when exactly one view names it; see `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces`.

mode.description: Layout: `inline` runs the fields together, `block` puts each on its own line.

omit_defaults.description: Leave assertions with `source: 'default'` out of the printed output. A print filter only: every condition in this format still sees the real, unfiltered state.

omit_empty.description: Skip empty fields. Defaults to true for `block`, false for `inline`.

Write a part's stand-in in place of the values it took from its whole.

A part that holds a stand-in (a concept that declares `stands_for_whole`) and was read against a whole holds the whole's values in the category the stand-in names. This format leaves those values out, so the part is written back with the word it was read with. It applies only to a part read on its own: a rollup is a whole, and is always written with its values. A print filter only, like `omit_defaults`: every condition in this format still sees the values.
