separator.description: Joins the nonempty top-level fields. Required once there is more than one field and no `joins` entry covers the boundary.

separator_aliases.description:
Spellings of this format's own separator that are read and never written.

The same word as on a field, said of the boundary between the format's top-level fields. See `FieldCommonDoc.separator_aliases`: tolerant pass only, never written, every use a `separator` correction, and no spelling here may be another field's separator or another field's prefix.

suffix.description: Written once after the nonempty whole.

surfaces.description: The scheme scope ids this format writes together, two or more and each once. Declared only in a scheme with `render.surfaces`. `surface` is absent.

view.description: Default concept view for fields that do not name one.

FormatDoc.description:
A format: one way this scheme's markings are written.

The field list is the canonical output order. It does not demand that input arrive in that order; the same tree recognizes a reordered marking and says what it corrected.

A format writes one surface, named in `surface`, or several at once, named in `surfaces`, when its syntax carries more than one part of a marking in one place, such as one XML attribute list. Exactly one of the two is declared. A format writes several surfaces only in a scheme that declares its outputs by surface in `render.surfaces`: without them every format is an output under its own id, and an output writes one surface.

GroupFieldDoc.description: A field made of ordered child fields.

attribute.description: `xml-attributes` syntax only: the attribute's local name.

fields.description: The children, in the order they are written.

joins.description: Separators for particular boundaries between adjacent children.

name.description: Human label for the field. Required on groups and alternatives, because a `joins` entry and a diagnostic both have to be able to name them.

prefix.description: Written once before the field's nonempty result.

prefix_aliases.description:
Spellings of this field's prefix that are read and never written.

A format writes one spelling of a line and documents in the wild carry more than one. A block whose classifier line opens `Classified By: ` also arrives spelled out for a derivative classifier, and a reader that accounts for every character refuses that spelling unless the format names it. Two `alternatives` that can both write one state are a conflict by design and never a winner by order, and a `Recognizer` describes a whole region rather than one line inside a block.

This is the tolerant half of the tree, written down. The canonical pass reads `prefix` and nothing else; a spelling named here is admitted only by the tolerant pass, beside the case difference, the declared alias, a concept's spelling in another of its views and the separator substitution it already admits, and every use is reported as an `alias` correction against the characters it read. The render side never reads this, which is what "never written" means. A format that declares none reads only `prefix`.

Only meaningful beside `prefix`, and no two fields of one format may claim one spelling, as a prefix or as an alias of one. A line that opens two fields is not a reading a format can settle, and nothing here is settled by declaration order.

required.description:
Whether the field standing empty is a state of this group at all.

Every field is optional by default, and on the read side that default is load-bearing in a way it is easy to miss: a group all of whose fields may stand empty reads any one of them on its own. A format that binds two categories beside a level therefore also reads a bare level, and becomes a rival account of text another format already reads whole. The alternative is not a tie-break, because nothing here is settled by declaration order, position or count. It is saying the thing the document could not say: a reading in which this field matched nothing is not a reading of this group.

Symmetric, because a representation that cannot be read is not one. Set here, the field is bound in every reading of the group that encloses it, and a state holding nothing for it is a state the group does not write: the group comes out empty, the facts its other fields would have carried are reported omitted, and another field or another format writes them. An omission, not a conflict: the group declined, and declining is what a format that does not represent a state is supposed to do.

The same word at a format's top level says it of the whole format, whose fields are one sequence. Inside `alternatives` it belongs to the option it is written in and says nothing about the others, because each option is a whole representation of the field and they do not share a reading.

It is a statement about this group's shape, never about the concept the field binds and never about whether a marking is well formed: a category that must be filled for a marking to make sense is `required` on the category, which is a different question with a different answer.

separator.description: What this field joins: its own values on a category field, its nonempty children on a group.

separator_aliases.description:
Spellings of this field's separator that are read and never written.

The sibling of `prefix_aliases`, one level down: a prefix says where a field opens and a separator says where one of its values ends, and a document in the wild spells the second as freely as the first. A list a format writes with `, ` arrives joined by `; ` or by a bare space, and a reader that accounts for every character reads the whole run as one value rather than quietly guessing a boundary.

Not the same as the substitutions the tolerant pass already makes. Those are spacing and de-doubling variants of the declared separator, and they deliberately invent no boundary the declared separator does not already put in the same place. This is the author saying that these other characters are that boundary, in this field, which is a statement only the document can make.

Tolerant pass only, never written, and every use is reported as a `separator` correction naming the characters read and the separator the format writes instead: the same correction a spacing substitution carries, because it is the same claim about the same boundary. The render side never reads this.

Only meaningful beside `separator`. A spelling named here may not be another field's declared separator or another field's prefix in the same format: a boundary that is also a field's own syntax is not a reading the format can settle, and nothing here is settled by declaration order.

suffix.description: Written once after the field's nonempty result.

view.description: Concept view for this field, overriding the enclosing view.

when.description: When this field applies. One predicate, read by both sides: the field is written only when it holds, and a reading of the input that would make it false is not a reading of this field.

InputAliasDoc.description:
An alias that only means this concept in a particular position.

The plain `aliases` list is unconditional. This one carries the condition the domain actually states, so a two-letter token that means one thing at the head of a marking and another after a category does not have to be guessed at by the engine. `position` is measured in the original recognized region, after any wrapper is stripped and before any reordering.

after_category.description: The category this text must follow, when that is the domain's rule.

position.description: Where in the marking region the text must appear.

text.description: The text recognized as this concept.

JoinDoc.description:
A boundary-specific separator: what is written between two named adjacent children of a group.

This is data about a boundary, not a change to either child's own separator. Naming two children that are not adjacent in `fields` is a compile error, so an author cannot declare an order the field list does not have.

A join is written only when both of the children it sits between produced something, which is the same rule every other separator in this contract follows: a separator joins nonempty results. An absent child takes the boundary before it with it rather than leaving a stray literal at the edge.

between.description: The two adjacent children, by `name` or by category id.

LayerBlockDoc.description:
The scheme family's layer payload. Required when `type: 'layer'`, forbidden otherwise, so layer-ness is never inferred from a combination of fields.

Binding and ordering are the cross-family rules: see `LayerBinding`.

## Three operations, the same for every element kind

- Add: declare an element whose id the stack below does not hold, in the section it normally lives in.
- Override: declare an element whose id the stack below already holds, complete. It replaces the one below in the same position.
- Remove: name it in `removes`. It stays gone until a later layer names it in `restores`, which brings back the definition it had below.

The element kinds, where each lives, and whether `removes` can name it:

| Kind              | Section                  | Removable | | ----------------- | ------------------------ | --------- | | `category`        | `data.categories`        | yes       | | `concept`         | `data.concepts.inline`   | yes       | | `external_source` | `data.concepts.external` | yes       | | `concept_group`   | `data.concept_groups`    | no        | | `scope`           | `scopes`                 | no        | | `named_condition` | `named_conditions`       | no        | | `recognizer`      | `parse.recognizers`      | yes       | | `repair_rule`     | `parse.normalize`        | yes       | | `rollup_pipeline` | `rollup_pipelines`       | yes       | | `render_format`   | `render.formats`         | yes       | | `render_surface`  | `render.surfaces`        | yes       | | `render_view`     | `render.surfaces.views`  | yes       | | `rule`            | `rules`                  | yes       | | `filter`          | `filters`                | no        | | `label_preset`    | `ui.label_presets`       | yes       | | `wizard_step`     | `ui.wizard_questions`    | no        |

A named condition is addressed by its key, an external source by its `id` (or `external-<n>`, its one-based position, when it has none), a render surface by its `surface`, a render view as `surface/view` with each id percent-encoded, and every other element by its `id`. Removing an external source takes the concepts it supplied with it. A header value that is not a collection (a name, a license, a parse or render setting, a `ui` setting) is not an element: a layer overrides it by stating it.

A render surface and each of its views are separate elements. A layer that states a surface the stack below holds overrides what belongs to the surface itself, its `default`, which it replaces whole, a view id or a map by role, and treats every view it lists as an element of its own: the view is added, or it overrides the view below with the same `surface/view`, complete, `role`, `format`, `cases` and `also_read_in` together, so a case list is replaced and never extended, and a view restated without a role has none. Views of that surface the layer does not list stay where they were.

## What a removal does to what names it

The stack behaves as if the removed element never existed, so whatever names it is narrowed, not dropped. A rule loses the removed member of a set (`when`, `target`, `rank`, `exclude`, `from`, a `with` table) and keeps the rest. A condition reads a removed concept as never present and a removed category as empty, and the surrounding `any`, `all` and `none` simplify around that. A concept that loses every category, or every parent, is removed. A rule is dropped only when its trigger can never hold, its target set is empty (an `exclusive` needs two members left), or the category it acts on is gone. Three actions keep a rule whose targets are gone. A `restrict` left with no targets stays and allows nothing in its category. A `require` or `require_any` that can no longer be met is never dropped: the stack takes its trigger away, or the stack is refused. A render format field bound to a removed element goes, along with any group or `joins` entry left with nothing to write. A view whose format is removed goes, as does a case or an `also_read_in` entry whose format is removed, and a surface left with no views goes too. A view takes its forms with it: when it goes, so does each format it names, as its `format`, in a case or in `also_read_in`, that no view left in the stack names. A restated view is not a removal: a format it stops naming that no other view in the stack names is refused at load, as any format no view names is, so the same layer removes that format or names it on a view. A surface that keeps some views but loses a view its default names, removed directly or with its format, is refused at load unless the same layer restates the surface with a default it still declares. A condition the removal leaves undecidable is refused at load with the element named; restate that element in the layer.

base.description: The artifact or layer this one stacks on, as `id@version`.

removes.description: Elements inherited from below that this layer takes away.

requires.description: Layers that must be present AND composed before this one. A layer that builds on what another layer introduced, or restores what another layer removed, only means anything on top of that layer, so the ordering is a load-time constraint rather than a hint.

restores.description: Elements an earlier layer removed that this one brings back, with the definition they had below. Naming an element in both `removes` and `restores` is a load error.

concept.description: The id of the concept to remove.

category.description: The id of the category to remove.

rule.description: The id of the scheme rule to remove.

recognizer.description: The id of the recognizer to remove.

repair_rule.description: The id of the repair rule to remove.

render_format.description: The id of the render format to remove.

render_surface.description: The id of the render surface to remove.

rollup_pipeline.description: The id of the rollup pipeline to remove.

label_preset.description: The id of the label preset to remove.

external_source.description: The id of the external concept source to remove.

LayerRemovalDoc.description:
One element a scheme layer takes away, named by kind and id. Exactly one key.

A reference rather than a path: `data.concepts.inline.X` would bake today's storage shape into every saved layer, and the collections are not uniformly addressable anyway. `{ concept: 'X' }` says what it means, survives a storage refactor, and validates as a closed set so a typo fails at load instead of silently removing nothing.

MarkingColorRuleDoc.description: A scheme-default display-color outcome chosen by a rule condition.

color.description: Complete background/text pair to apply when the condition matches.

when.description: Rule condition, in the same `when` syntax scheme rules use. Omit only on the final entry to create an unconditional/anything-else fallback.

NamedConditionRefDoc.description: A reference to a reusable condition declared in `scheme.named_conditions`.

named_condition.description: Named-condition ID from this document or from a base/required layer.

NormalizeRuleDoc.description: A single normalize/repair rule: input rewrite during parse.

correction.description: The correction to apply, read per type: replacement text for `separator`, and for `case` the grammar's canonical case, `'upper'` (the default) or `'lower'`.

pattern.description: Detection or match regex, read per type: for `case` it selects the input that needs correcting; for `separator` it matches the text to replace.

OutputCaseDoc.description: A guarded alternative to a view's format.

format.description: The format written while this case holds. It must write the view's surface.

when.description: When this case holds, evaluated against the whole state of the operation.

OutputViewDoc.description:
A named view of one surface: an output a caller can ask for by id, and what text is read as.

A view is written in its `format`, or in a case's format while that case holds, and is read in those and in each format `also_read_in` lists. Those are the view's forms, though a request that names the view as its input format reads only the ones the view writes, as `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states. Every format of a scheme that declares `render.surfaces` is a form of one view on each surface it serves, so text read in a form on one surface is read as that surface's view, and has the view's role.

A view `full` that is a whole, written in `full_line` and still read in the retired `full_line_2019`, is `{ id: full, role: whole, format: full_line, also_read_in: [full_line_2019] }`.

A view id names an output, not a concept spelling. Two views can write through formats that spell concepts the same way, and a format's concept `view` needs no output named after it.

also_read_in.description:
Formats this view is also read in and never written in, such as a spelling the scheme retired but still reads in older documents.

Each is a format of the view's surface, listed once, that no other view of that surface names. None is the view's `format` or a case's format, which the view is read in already.

They are read when a request names no input format, or names one of them by its own id. A request that names this view reads only the forms this view writes, as `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states.

cases.description:
Conditions under which another format writes this output instead.

Cases are alternatives, not a priority list. Every case is evaluated against the whole state of the operation: exactly one holding selects its format, none holding selects `format`, and more than one holding, or one that cannot be decided, refuses the output rather than picking for it.

format.description: The format written when no case holds. It must write the view's surface.

id.description: View id, unique within its surface.

role.description:
The role of the markings this is a view of.

Text read as this view is a marking of this role, so a request about it that names no output and no context role is written in its surface's default for this role. Absent, the view has no role, as an attribute list or a block that is neither a whole nor a part has none, and text read as it has none either.

Text read in a form has one role, so the views on other surfaces that name one of this view's forms state the role this view states, or no role when this view states none.

ParseConfigDoc.description:
Parse configuration: recognition policy, exceptional recognizers, and the repair rules applied before recognition.

No tokenizer settings. Every boundary in a marking belongs to the field that writes it, so there is no global separator to declare here and nothing for a split exception to be an exception to.

case_sensitive.description:
Whether the vocabulary is matched case-sensitively.

Recognition policy, not lexing: every boundary in a marking belongs to the field that writes it, and this says how a spelling found at one of those boundaries is compared against the vocabulary. Default false.

recognizers.description: Declarations for input no field tree can describe.

strip_whitespace.description:
Whether surrounding whitespace is ignored when a spelling is compared.

Recognition policy, like `case_sensitive`. It does not split anything; it decides whether the space an author left around a value keeps that value from being recognized. Default true.

PhraseDoc.description:
One concept of a field's category, written together with the fields that belong to it.

A category's own order says where each of its concepts is written. Some of them introduce something: a release control is written with the countries it releases to, and the control and the list are one phrase rather than two fields that happen to be adjacent. Written as two fields, the list has to sit somewhere in the format's own sequence, and the rest of the category has to sit beside it, which means the format has decided, once, whether the plain controls come before the list or after. A register that writes one control before the list and another after it has no such answer, and neither choice is right for more than half of them.

A phrase is the sentence that says it. The head is a concept of this field's category, so the category's order already places it, and the phrase is written at the head's position among the field's other values. Nothing else moves: the plain controls keep their own places, before or after, because the order decides and no field had to know where a control sits.

Read back as one unit, for the same reason. The head and its fields are one value of this field, so a reading that takes the head without its list, or the list without its head, is not a reading of this phrase.

The head is excluded from the field's plain values automatically. It is written here, and `exclude_concepts` is for a concept another field writes.

fields.description: The fields written with the head.

head.description: The concept of this field's category that heads the phrase, and whose position in that category's order the phrase is written at.

head_position.description: Where the head sits relative to its fields. `first` by default, which is a heading; `last` is the list that names its control afterwards.

separator.description: What joins the head to its fields, and the fields to each other.

after.description: The concept this one renders after.

before.description: The concept this one renders before.

between.description: The two concepts this one renders between, in either order.

PositionSpecDoc.description:
Position spec for a concept: where it renders among the concepts of its category.

- `'first'` / `'last'`: ahead of or behind every other position.
- Number: absolute position; lower renders earlier.
- `{ after: <id> }`: renders after the named concept.
- `{ before: <id> }`: renders before the named concept.
- `{ between: [a, b] }`: renders between the two named concepts.

`before` mirrors `after`: `A: { before: B }` orders the pair exactly as `B: { after: A }` does. A relative spec names a concept of the same category. A name that resolves to no concept places this one last and reports a warning; relative specs that form a cycle are a load error.

ProcessingRole.description: Structural role of a marking within a processing operation.

above.description: The concept this one ranks above.

below.description: The concept this one ranks below.

between.description: The two concepts this one ranks between, in either order.

RankSpecDoc.description:
Rank spec for a concept: its severity for rank-based rollup (max, min, least_upper_bound).

- `'top'` / `'bottom'`: highest or lowest rank.
- Number: absolute rank; higher is more severe.
- `{ above: <id> }`: more severe than the named concept.
- `{ below: <id> }`: less severe than the named concept.
- `{ between: [a, b] }`: between the two named concepts.

`below` mirrors `above`: `A: { below: B }` ranks the pair exactly as `B: { above: A }` does. A relative spec names a ranked concept of the same category. A name that resolves to no ranked concept gives this one the top rank, failing closed, and reports a warning; relative specs that form a cycle are a load error.

RecognizerDoc.description:
A declaration for input a format's field tree genuinely cannot describe.

The ordinary case needs none of these. A format's fields already say what the marking is made of, and recognition reads that same tree, so a phrase group, a typed value, a view, and an alias all recognize themselves. What is left is the rare shape whose spelling carries no vocabulary at all.

Deliberately narrow. One pattern, no variants, no priority: a recognizer proposes candidate bindings into the same evidence graph, under the same work budgets, competing on evidence like everything else. It never asserts a concept directly, and it never runs as a second pass after a canonical read has failed, because a fallback that only fires on failure is a way of turning an unrecognized input into a confident one.

binds.description: Capture group to field name, within `format`.

field.description: Name of the field in `format` that receives the captured text.

case_sensitive.description:
Whether this pattern reads case as a difference.

Absent, the pattern follows `parse.case_sensitive`, which is the policy the vocabulary beside it is compared under: one scheme, one answer to the question of whether a spelling in the wrong case is the same spelling. Present, it overrides that policy for this pattern alone, for the declaration whose shape genuinely is case-bearing when the rest of the scheme's is not. There is no flags string: a pattern carrying its own flag could read case one way while the vocabulary it feeds read it the other, and nothing said which was meant.

format.description: The format whose field tree these captures feed.

message.description: Human-readable explanation surfaced with the recognition.

pattern.description: One bounded pattern from the supported regex subset.

RenderConfigDoc.description: Render configuration: the formats a scheme reads and writes, and, when it declares them by surface, the outputs it offers.

color_from.description: Display-color source. A category ID takes its color from the resolved concept in that single-valued category. An ordered rule array supports compound defaults; first matching rule wins. The two modes are mutually exclusive.

default.description: ID of the format used when none is specified. Not declared beside `surfaces`, where each surface names its own default view.

of_invalid.description: Render-of-invalid policy: how the renderer treats input tokens that match no concept. `preserve_unmatched` (the default) echoes them through to the output; `drop_unmatched` discards them; `refuse` renders nothing for an invalid marking. Consumed by the engine's scheme-mapper (D8).

refusal_marker.description: What the `refuse` policy renders in place of the marking. The optional `{tokens}` placeholder is replaced with the comma-joined unmatched tokens. Defaults to `[INVALID MARKING: unrecognized {tokens}]`. Only consulted when `of_invalid` is `refuse`.

surface_separator.description: Written between the outputs of two surfaces when one rendered string carries both, unless their syntax merges them, as attributes on one XML element do. Required when `surfaces` lists more than one surface, and not declared without `surfaces`.

surfaces.description:
Named outputs per surface. When declared, these are the scheme's outputs and `formats` is the library of their forms: every format is a form of one view on each surface it serves, written by that view or only read in for it. A format that a surface it serves has no view for is refused, and so is one named by two views of a surface. The views that name one format on different surfaces state one role between them, or none, because text read in a form has one role. Results are keyed by output address, `surface/view`, one entry per view, surfaces in this order and views in theirs.

Text is read as a view of the surface whose categories it carries. Recognition settles the facts first, and views never change what they are. It then decides the view among the views of that surface whose forms read those facts:

- The one view with a form that writes the text exactly as given.
- Failing that, the one view with a form that read every token in its own spelling.
- Failing that, a role: among the views still tied (those with a form that writes the text exactly, else those with a form that read every token in its own spelling, else every view whose forms read the facts), when all are of one role, that role, with the role's default view when it is one of them.
- Otherwise no view and no role.

Where a view is decided, recognition takes its corrections from a form of that view, so no correction points at another view's spelling. Text a form writes exactly is not corrected, whether or not one view is decided.

Text that carries the categories of more than one surface, in one form views of those surfaces share or in parts read in different forms, is read as no one view. Each surface's part of it is decided as a view on its own, as above, and takes its corrections from the view decided for it. The text's role is the one those parts agree on, counting only the parts that have a role: a part read as a view with no role, or with no role decided, leaves the role to the others.

What the engine writes for a valid marking, on one surface or several, must read back as right as written: `inputWasValid` is true, nothing is corrected, and the same output writes the same text again.

Recognition reports the view in `recognition.inputFormat`, its surface in `recognition.surface` and the role in `recognition.role`, each only when it is decided, and never the form the text happened to be read in.

A result writes the surfaces its input was read on: those of the categories it asserted, before or after repair, together with the surface a request's `surface` field names and the surfaces of the view or format a request names as its input format. With none of those it writes the default scope's surface, so the default scope is always one of the surfaces listed here. A fact inferred afterwards adds no surface. Neither does a request's output format: it only chooses how those surfaces are written, so `surface/view` for a surface the result does not write selects nothing there.

When a request names no output, each surface the result writes is written in its default for the marking's role: the view its `default` names for that role, or the one view it names for every role. The role is the request's context role when it gives one. Otherwise it is the role recognition decides for the text, the one `recognition.role` reports. Text whose role is not decided has no role, and neither has a marking given as facts with no context role. A marking with no role is written as a whole. An aggregate's rollup is a whole and is written as one; the context role an aggregate request gives describes the parts it reads. This is the one rule for an unnamed output, and every operation follows it but a scan, which keeps a marking it finds in the view it was read as when that view writes the form it was read in, and writes each one in the output its `ScanResult.type` names. Wherever the list below says a surface writes its default, it is this default for the marking's role.

Wherever a request takes an output format, it names one of these:

- A view id, such as `full`. Every surface the result writes uses that view, and a surface that does not declare it writes its default.
- `surface/view`. That surface writes that view, or its default when it declares no view by that id, and every other surface writes its default. A surface this list does not declare is refused, never guessed.
- The id of a format that exactly one view names as one of its forms, written or only read. It stands for that view's `surface/view`.

A view id wins over a format id spelled the same way, so a bare `x` that is a view of one surface and a form of another surface's view asks every surface for view `x`. A declared surface id, or a format that views on several surfaces name, names no output: every surface writes its default, as it does when the request names no output. An undeclared id is refused; it is never answered as though the request had named none.

Wherever a request takes an input format, it names what the text is read as:

- A view id. The text is read in the forms the views by that id write, each one's `format` and case formats, on every surface that declares one, and in no other format.
- `surface/view`. The text is read in the forms that view writes only.
- The id of a format. The text is read in that form alone.

A form a view is only read in, one its `also_read_in` lists, is read when the request names no input format, or names that form by its own id. Naming the view does not read it: a view's written forms are how it spells a marking, and a form it is only read in is a spelling the scheme still tolerates, not one the view stands for.

A view id wins over a format id spelled the same way here too, and any other id is refused. Whatever the request names, recognition reports the view the text was read as, decided as above among the views it allows.

Each id in an address is percent-encoded the way `encodeURIComponent` encodes it, in requests and in result keys alike, so an id may hold a `/`. An address is split on its one literal `/` before its parts are decoded, and one with more than one literal `/` or a malformed escape is refused. Every field that carries an output address (the keys of `renders`, `RenderFormatLayout.id`, `FormatView.id`, `defaultRenderFormat` and the role defaults, `ScanResult.type`, `recognition.inputFormat`, `UnrepresentableOutput.output`) holds the same encoded string.

Absent, every format is an output under its own id and `default` picks one. The two are not combined.

RepairConfidence.description: Confidence assigned to a deterministic repair.

RollupPipelineDoc.description: A rollup pipeline: resolves one or more pipeline-rolled categories.

categories.description: Category IDs resolved together by this pipeline.

steps.description: Pipeline steps. Evaluation order depends on `mode`.

RollupPipelineStepDoc.description: A rollup-pipeline step: conditional then/else block evaluated in order.

else.description: Else-block: applied when `when` does not match.

then.description: Then-block: how to combine and remove concepts when this step fires.

when.description: Trigger condition for this step. Omit for unconditional fallback step.

RuleActionDoc.description:
Rule actions recognized by the engine.

Three of them say which of the targets a marking must or may hold:

- `require`: every target must be present. When the rule names `category`, the targets are added there.
- `require_any`: at least one target must be present, in `category` when the rule names one and anywhere in the marking otherwise. It only checks; it never adds a value.
- `restrict`: `category` may hold only the targets. The rule must name `category`, and an empty category satisfies it. Permissive processing removes the values the targets do not allow.

One of them only advises:

- `warn`: when the rule's `when` holds, the result carries its `message` as a warning. The marking stays exactly as it was: nothing is added or removed, the rendering does not change, and `valid` is decided by the other rules alone. A `warn` rule needs a `message` and names no `target`, `category` or other operand, because it acts on nothing.

RuleConditionTarget.description:
Assertion set a rule condition is evaluated against.

- `'self'` (default): the assertions currently under evaluation.
- `'context'`: the assertions of the whole marking this one is part of. Such a condition has an answer only when the part has a verified whole, one that reads and is valid. Without one (no whole given, a whole that does not read, or a whole that reads but is invalid) the condition is unresolved, and so is any `all`, `any` or `none` around it whose answer depends on it. A rule whose `when` is unresolved never fires, changes no value, reports no error and offers no fix; a check rule (`require`, `require_any`, `restrict`, `forbid`, `exclusive`, `cardinality`) that the marking already meets still passes, and any other unresolved rule gives the part the `_whole_unverified` notice.
- `'contributors'`: each contributing assertion set that went into an aggregate, evaluated separately. The condition holds only when EVERY contributor satisfies it, and it is never satisfied outside aggregation, where there are no contributors to inspect. Use it to describe what must be true of every part of a document, which the merged set can no longer answer once the parts have been collapsed into one.

RuleContributorQuantifier.description: Quantifies a condition block over contributing assertion sets.

RuleTargetSelectorDoc.description:
A rule target that names concepts by where they sit in the hierarchy rather than one by one. Each form is a member of this union: `ChildrenOfSelectorDoc`.

A selector is a target of `require_any`, `forbid` and `restrict`, the actions that ask whether one of a set is present, keep a set out, or keep a category to a set. Any other action refuses it at load.

SchemeBlock.description: The body inside the top-level `scheme:` envelope.

default_scope.description:
The scope a marking is in when nothing names one: one of `scopes`, by id.

Required whenever a scheme declares at least one scope, and the only way to name the default: the scheme names its default scope once, as a surface names its default view. A layer may leave it out and keep the default of the stack it sits on, or state it to name another; a layer that gives the stack its first scopes names one.

definition.description: Official description or definition of this scheme.

deprecated.description: Whether this scheme as a whole is deprecated.

deprecated_since.description: Date the scheme was deprecated, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

description.description: Longer description of what this scheme covers.

guidance.description: Usage notes, restrictions, or guidelines for this scheme.

layer.description: The scheme family's layer payload. Required when `type: 'layer'`, forbidden otherwise.

license.description: License label shown with the scheme, such as `enterprise`. Informational only: it does not grant or restrict use.

named_conditions.description: Reusable `when` trees referenced with `{ named_condition: <id> }`. A layer may also reference definitions inherited from its base and required layers.

part_scope.description: How much text a part marking governs in a document audit: `'paragraph'` (default, the mark's own line(s)), `'until-next'` (through to the next part marking, a section style), or `'document'`. Lets schemes that place/scope markings differently audit correctly. Maps to runtime `Scheme.partScope`.

replaced_by.description: Scheme id that supersedes this one.

role_aware.description: When true, this scheme reads a marking in the role its context gives, and a part's rules can read the whole it is part of. Whether or not it is, `process`, `validate` and `explain` compare a part that is valid on its own with a whole that reads and is valid.

role_detection.description:
When a marking in each role is required and, for a scheme without `render.surfaces`, the formats each role is read in.

A role's `required_when` condition evaluates after discovery against authored whole assertions and authored part contributors. Omitted, a whole is optional and a part required. Named conditions use the same scheme condition registry.

A scheme that declares `render.surfaces` lists no formats here: each of its views states its own `role`, and a role is read in the forms of the views that state it. A role takes `{ required_when: ... }` and nothing else, and a list, flat or under `views`, is refused.

A scheme without `render.surfaces` lists the format ids each role is read in, in one of two shapes:

- Flat: `{ whole: ['full'], part: ['wrapped'] }`.
- Nested: `{ whole: { views: [...] }, part: { views: [...] } }`: the same list under `views`, beside an optional `required_when`.

Either way the lists are about reading. The view or format a marking in each role is written in, when a request names none, comes from the surface's `default`, or from `render.default`. A role entry that says nothing is refused.

required_when.description: The condition under which a part marking is required.

views.description: The format ids a part marking is read in.

part.description: How a part marking is detected.

required_when.description: The condition under which a whole marking is required.

views.description: The format ids a whole marking is read in.

whole.description: How a whole marking is detected.

rollup_pipelines.description: Rollup pipelines for categories with `rollup: pipeline`.

rules.description: Scheme rules: conditions and the actions they trigger.

scope_label.description: Display label for the scope selector.

scopes.description: Scope definitions, in the order a selector offers them.

tier.description: Distribution tier this document belongs to. Names which catalog carries it; it grants nothing and is read by packaging, not by the engine.

type.description:
What kind of document this is. Absent means `'scheme'`.

The single discriminator for layer-ness: `type: 'layer'` requires the `layer` block and `type: 'scheme'` forbids it, both enforced at load.

Every layerable family wears this same envelope; see `LayerBinding`.

ui.description: UI metadata: engine knows `label_presets` and `wizard_questions`; other keys opaque. `vocabulary` is a top-level SchemeBlock field, not a `ui` sub-key, so it is schema-validated the same way as guide's and access's.

vocabulary.description: Display-term overrides consulted by runtime UI components. Same shape and chokepoint as guide's and access's own top-level `vocabulary` block: an open map from a term key to a `{ singular, plural }` pair (or a bare `singular`, auto-pluralized). Reserved scheme keys are `handbook`, which renames the scheme's reference surface, and `whole` / `part`, which name the structural context roles. For example: `{ handbook: { singular: "Register" }, whole: { singular: "banner" } }`.

SchemeConceptsBlock.description:
Inline-or-external concepts block: the canonical 1.0 wire shape for a scheme's concept set, per the Context-with-sources schema.

When a concept in `inline` and a record from one of this block's `external` sources have the same id, the inline concept is the one used, for reading, writing, suggesting, describing, validating and judging coverage. The source's record for that id is not used, and assertions of the concept carry no `provenance`. This is how an author overrides one record of a source they do not control. Among external sources, the first source that supplies an id is the one used.

Those two rules settle a collision inside one scheme document. Across the documents of a layered stack, layer precedence decides first: a colliding id means the later declaration wins (see `LayerBinding`), and a concept an `external` source supplies counts as declared by the document that declares the source. So when a later layer's source supplies a concept that an earlier document in the stack declares `inline`, the later layer's record is the one used. Inline-over-external never reaches back across layers. The same holds the other way round, and between two sources declared in different layers.

external.description: Live external sources. An array allows a scheme to draw concepts from multiple upstream endpoints; the loader rejects a bare (non-array) source spec.

inline.description: Inline concepts: a flat array of `ConceptDoc`, each carrying its own `id`. Matches the `rules.inline` shape on guides and access docs.

SchemeDataDoc.description:
The `data` block: categories and concepts.

`concepts` is the `SchemeConceptsBlock` with `inline` and `external` peers; the loader rejects any other shape.

concept_groups.description: Named groupings of concepts, for organizing them in a UI or in docs.

SchemeRuleDoc.description: A scheme rule: a trigger condition, an action, and action-specific parameters.

action.description: What to do when the rule fires.

category.description:
Target category: disambiguates multi-category concepts or specifies the operating category.

A `restrict` rule requires it: it is the category the rule restricts to the targets. On a `require_any` rule it says where a target must appear.

citation.description:
Where in the governing document this rule was read from. Free text, e.g. `32 CFR 2002.20(b)(1)`.

Provenance only: nothing parses it, matches on it, or renders it. Distinct from `explanation` (what the rule does) and `message` (what a violation tells the author).

exclude.description: For move: concept ID to exclude from the move.

explanation.description: Human-readable explanation of what this rule does.

formats.description: Render formats the rule applies to, by format id. Absent means all.

from.description: Source category ID(s). String for copy/move/inherit_parents, array for intersect/union.

id.description: Unique rule identifier within the scheme. An id that begins with `_` is refused: the engine keeps that prefix for its own ids, the ones it reports its own errors under as `constraintId` and writes as `sourceRule` on assertions its structure added.

message.description: Validation error message for the constraint actions (forbid, require, require_any, restrict, exclusive, cardinality), and the warning a `warn` rule gives, which it requires.

name.description: Human-readable rule name for UI and audit provenance.

phases.description:
Evaluation contexts the rule runs in. Absent means every one of them.

These are the contexts the engine actually asks about, not a parallel naming of the pipeline:

- `pre-merge`: each input set on its own, before rollup, and a standalone `process()` call
- `post-merge`: the merged whole, after rollup
- `validate`: an explicit `validate()` call
- `render`: the render-time visibility check
- `suggest`: suggestion generation

Inclusion only. A rule that names contexts runs in those and no others; there is no `!` form, because the closed list makes the complement writable and one way to say a thing keeps a scope readable.

rank.description: For exclusive: priority among derived concepts during repair or rollup (first = highest priority). Repair preserves author-stated concepts.

surfaces.description: Surfaces the rule applies to, as scheme scope ids. A leading `!` excludes one. Absent means every surface.

target.description: What the action acts on: a concept or category id, a list of them, or a selector such as `{ children_of: PROGRAM }` that names concepts by their place in the hierarchy. See `RuleTargetSelectorDoc`.

with.description: For supersede: what replaces the target.

envVar.description: Name of the environment variable that holds the secret.

provider.description: Read the secret from an environment variable.

certVar.description: Environment variable that holds the PEM certificate.

keyVar.description: Environment variable that holds the PEM private key.

provider.description: Read a certificate and key pair from two environment variables.

path.description: Path of the file that holds the secret. It must lie under a file root the deployment allows.

provider.description: Read the secret from a mounted file.

certPath.description: Path of the PEM certificate file, under an allowed file root.

keyPath.description: Path of the PEM private key file, under an allowed file root.

provider.description: Read a certificate and key pair from two mounted files.
Ask the deployment's secret store for the secret.

secretId.description: The id of the secret in that store.

SecretRefDoc.description:
A reference to a piece of secret material, never the material itself. `provider` says where the server finds it when the source issues a request: `env` reads an environment variable (or a certificate and key pair of them), `file` reads a mounted file (or a certificate and key pair of files), and `secret-store` asks the secret store the deployment names for the secret with that id.

Browsers never see raw secrets, only the reference. The material stays on the server that resolves it.

SurfaceOutputDoc.description:
The outputs one surface offers: its named views, in order, and the one it writes when a request does not choose.

A surface `sensitivity` whose everyday view is `full`, whose part markings are written `short`, and which also writes `xml` for a caller that asks for it by name declares those three views, `full` a whole and `short` a part, and `default: { whole: full, part: short }`. A surface `retention` with one view, `block`, declares `default: block`. A request for a view a surface does not declare gets that surface's default for the marking's role.

default.description:
The view written when a request names none, or names one this surface does not declare: a view id, or a view per role.

A view id means every marking is written in that view, whatever its role. That is all a surface with one view, or one right default for every marking, needs. A `DefaultViewByRoleDoc` names the view for a whole and, when it differs, for a part. Either way each view named is one of `views`, the same way `render.default` is always one of `render.formats`.

A surface that has views of a role writes a marking of that role in one of them. A default that would write it in a view of another role, or of none, is refused there: a view id that is not of that role, a map value that is not, or a `whole` that a part falls back to.

surface.description: The scheme scope id these outputs write.

views.description: The views a caller can ask for, in display and result order.

escape.description: How a character the syntax cannot frame is escaped.

namespace.description: Namespace to write the attributes in, when the format has one.

prefix.description: The namespace prefix the attributes are written with.

uri.description: The namespace URI the prefix is bound to.

SyntaxDoc.description: How a format's text is framed: its encoding, not its layout.

plural.description: The word for more than one, such as `rules`.

singular.description: The word for one, such as `rule`.

TextInputDoc.description: Free-text input configuration for a concept that accepts user-typed text.

encoding.description: How the value is spelled and stored. Absent means plain text.

label.description: Display label for the text input in forms.

placeholder.description: Hint text shown in the UI input field.

recognition.description: Hint for locating this concept's free text when nothing has bound it.

required.description: Whether a value must be provided (default true).

TextInputRecognitionDoc.description:
A hint for finding free text that no field has bound yet.

It helps recognition locate the start of an unlabeled run of text. It is not a constraint on the language of a field that is already bound: an event description supplied explicitly is still an event description whatever word it opens with.

begins_with_word.description: Words that may open an unbound run of this concept's free text.

TierCompositionDoc.description:
How a tiered concept composes inside one field: what attaches a tier level to the one above it, and the view each half of the composed token is written in.

The composition rule belongs to the field that writes the category, not to the whole format, because two fields may legitimately write the same tier family differently. A concept that declares the tier view uses it; one that does not keeps the field's view.

A composed token has two halves and they are not obliged to agree. The head is the level being composed with; the child is the level this entry governs. A format that spells its concepts out in full may still want the head short inside a composed token, because the composed form is a name in its own right and the spelled-out head reads as a sentence rather than a marking. `view` sets the child's; `head_view` sets the head's; the field's view is what either falls back to. Neither reaches the head written on its own, which is not part of a composed token and keeps the field's view like any other value.

attached_by.description:
What attaches this tier level to the one it composes with.

Not `separator`. Everywhere else in this contract a separator joins siblings: a field's values, a group's children, a format's fields. This is a child-to-parent boundary. Reading "the subprogram tier's separator is a hyphen" aloud does not say which boundary is meant, and a reader who knows the rest of the contract guesses the wrong one. "The subprogram tier is attached by a hyphen" says it.

head_view.description:
View for the composed token's head, the level this one composes with.

Absent means the field's view, which is the head written the same way it is written standing alone. Naming a view here changes the head only inside a composed token: the same concept written on its own is a value of this field like any other and is unaffected.

tier.description: The tier label this entry governs.

view.description: View for the composed token's child; falls back to the field's view.

max_length.description: Reject a value longer than this many characters.

pattern.description:
A validation constraint on the value: it is rejected unless the whole value matches. Anchoring is implicit and total, so a partial match is a rejection.

This is not a recognition device and never becomes one. It does not tell the reader where this concept's text starts or ends, it does not compete with any other reading, and nothing is extracted from it: the value is found by the field that binds it and then checked against this.

A pattern that describes a shape belongs in `calendar-date` or `composite`, which say how to write the value again as well as how to read it.

type.description: Plain text, stored exactly as supplied.

canonical.description: The spelling the value is stored in.

type.description: A calendar date: a real year, month and day, with leap years and month lengths enforced. Never a timestamp, never timezone-shifted.

views.description: Per-view output spelling; views not named here use `canonical`.

fields.description: The components, in the order they are written.

type.description: An ordered set of components stored as one normalized string.

ValueEncodingDoc.description:
How a free-text value is spelled on the wire and how it is stored.

A codec, not a validator: every encoding states both directions, so a value this contract accepts is a value the contract can write back. A bare regex declares what may be read and says nothing about how to print the stored value again, which is why no encoding takes a regex.

Vocabulary.description:
Author-facing vocabulary: an open map from a term key (e.g. "rule", "concept", "tag") to the display words. Term keys are not enumerated here; consumers pick the keys that matter to them.

Purely a presentation hint: nothing in the engine's evaluation logic reads it. Each consumer owns its own default map and calls `resolveVocabulary(source, defaults)` to merge.

WhenDoc.description:
A rule's `when:` field: the trigger condition.

Forms accepted by the loader:

- String: concept ID that must be present.
- Array of strings: any-of concept IDs.
- Array of conditions: implicit all-of (every condition must hold).
- Object with `{any|all|none}` quantifiers and/or `{category: X}` shorthand.

WhenQuantifierDoc.description: A nested boolean block in a rule's `when:` tree.

any.description: Quantifier: at least one item must hold. Items are conditions or nested quantifiers.

category.description: Category-shorthand: any concept in this category triggers the rule.

quantifier.description: Combine contributor results using any, all (default), or none. Valid only with target: contributors. A missing or empty contributor set never satisfies the block, including when quantifier is all or none.

scope.description: Restrict the contexts in which this `when` block applies. Recognized context names include `'render'` and `'suggest'`. Omit (or use the array form of `when:`) to apply in every context.

target.description: Evaluate the complete boolean expression separately for each contributor.
